headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Devin’s broad write/network/MCP access can feed LangGraph workflows that may act on unverified outputs, creating dangerous default-path conflicts and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can read/write cloud workspace files and use MCP, while LangGraph can ingest developer-defined tools and application-defined files. That creates a plausible shared-channel injection path if LangGraph workflows consume Devin-authored content as instructions. The interaction is not proven, so I avoid high, but the pathway exists in default-style integrations.
conditions: IF LangGraph reads Devin-produced files or tool outputs as prompts or instructions
IF a shared MCP server or workspace is wired between the two agents
mitigations: Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in the handoff format
Require allowlisted schemas for any Devin-to-LangGraph payload
Disable MCP bridging between the agents for the first run
Log and review one sample handoff before enabling automation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets, and has broad network egress plus Slack/Jira/Notion writes. LangGraph can pass application-defined state to model providers and developer-defined tools. If Devin’s workspace data is routed into LangGraph state, sensitive material can leak across systems in default configurations.
conditions: IF Devin outputs are copied into LangGraph state containing sensitive code or chat
IF LangGraph tools forward that state to external model providers or APIs
mitigations: Redact secrets before any Devin-to-LangGraph transfer
Use a minimal state object with no raw file contents
Turn off external tool calls for the first workflow run
Verify one end-to-end trace for secret leakage

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad cloud-workspace shell access; LangGraph also has write_filesystem and can drive developer-defined tools. Both can mutate shared resources, and Devin’s shared_state_with_other_instances plus LangGraph’s checkpointer store make concurrent writes plausible. Without explicit locking, default overlap can corrupt state or git history.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repo, workspace, or checkpointer namespace
IF either agent modifies git state without an external lock
mitigations: Assign separate directories or repos per agent
Add a mutex around git and checkpoint writes
Run one agent read-only during the other’s write phase
Use branch-per-agent with mandatory merge review

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor, and LangGraph is a graph of nodes where each node may itself be an agent. That makes it plausible for LangGraph to treat Devin’s outputs as authoritative and then trigger downstream actions through developer-defined tools. The pair can therefore amplify a single bad output into real actions unless verification is added.
conditions: IF LangGraph routes Devin output directly into action-taking nodes
IF no verification or human approval step exists between generation and execution
mitigations: Insert a verification node before any side-effecting action
Require human approval for emails, commits, or ticket writes
Have LangGraph compare Devin output against a second source
Disable downstream action nodes until the workflow is tested

E_compliance.rationale: Devin explicitly handles source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets, while LangGraph stores application-defined graph state and can send data to model providers. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into LangGraph state, retention and residency obligations may diverge. I cite both because the mismatch arises from their combined data flow, not either agent alone.
conditions: IF regulated data is included in LangGraph state or tool inputs
IF the model provider or tool chain has different retention or residency terms than Devin’s workspace
mitigations: Classify data before routing it into LangGraph
Keep regulated data out of shared graph state
Review retention settings for model providers and tools
Document a deletion/export path for shared workflow data
